svg.aria-label: a torn commit replays the prefix and over-counts
svg.text: Checkpointing a stateful processor — the full cycle
23 loaded + 22 replayed = 45 · local store vs durable checkpoint
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being aggregated · key = which group it belongs to
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds of event time. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: KEYS — the keys state is held per. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
12 // primitive: CHK — the index the checkpoint in this chapter was taken at. CHK = 4
13 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the window holding et.
15 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
16 // primitive: contains(xs, x) — is x in xs? contains([1,2], 2) = true
17 // primitive: watermarkAfter(i) — highest event time through i, minus LAG.
24 // primitive: entryOf(e) — the (key, window) pair this event belongs to.
26 // primitive: PREFIX_V — the v inside the checkpoint at CHK. PREFIX_V = 23
28 // function: applyTo(store, e) — the processor's whole steady-state behaviour.
29 // applyTo(a fresh store, EVENTS[0]) sets entries["a@0"] : 0 -> 5
37 // primitive: copyOf(m) — a snapshot of the map, not a reference to it.
40 // function: commit(store, offset, atomic) — write the state and the offset to
41 // DURABLE storage. The local store survives a restart; it does not survive the
42 // machine, which is why this exists at all.
44 // commit(store, CHK, false) may land the state WITHOUT the offset
47 if (atomic == false) { cp.offset = 0 } // crashed between the two writes
50 // primitive: countOf(m) — how many keys the map has. countOf(the full state) = 7
52 // function: resume(cp) — load the state, seek to the offset, replay the rest.
53 // resume(commit(store, CHK, true)).total = 45 resume(commit(store, CHK, false)).total = 68
62 for (id in store.entries) { total = total + store.entries[id] }
65 // function: main() — THE CALLER: run, checkpoint, crash, resume — twice.
68 for (i in 0 .. CHK) { store = applyTo(store, EVENTS[i]) }
Step 4/0 — a torn commit replays the prefix and over-counts
With `atomic` false the entries landed and the offset did not, so `resume` replays from index 1 and `torn.total` reaches 68 — over by the whole 23 the checkpoint already
held. The design REQUIRES this commit to be atomic and does not itself provide that.
